4. Defendant No. 1 appeared in the suit but did not file any written statement. The suit was dismissed ex-parte by judgment and decree dated 22.8.89. Thereafter the petitioner preferred an appeal before the High Court Division against the afore-said judgment and decree through her constituted attorney being First Appeal No. 143 of 1989 which is pending. 

 He submits that the appeal is the continuation of the suit and when admittedly in the suit a declaration has been sought for by the petitioner challenging, long before the property in question is not an abandoned property and not vested in the Government and in view of the proviso (b) of the Ordinance aforesaid the listing of the property as abandoned is absolutely illegal, without jurisdiction and of no leg effect. The learned Advocate for the petitioner placed before us the photocopy of the judgment and decree of the First Appeal No. 143 of 1989 of this Court arising out of Title Suit No. 86 of 1987 where-in a Division Bench of this court by its judgment and decree dated 7.12.95 allowed the appeal declaring the title of the petitioner in the suit property and the notices issued under order bearing No. XVII/Dacca-9/79/330 dated 28.5.80 as illegal, arbitrary, void and of no legal effect -and not binding upon the petitioner. The learned Advocate lastly contends that the law is settled now that without going to the court. of Settlement a person for protection of his property as guaranteed under Article 42 of our Constitution can come .to this court under Article 102 of the Constitution. In support of his contention he referred the case of Saleha Khatun Vs. The Chairman, 1st Court of Settlement and another, reported in. 49 DLR (HCD). 243 relevant para 6 wherein it has been held: 

 8. Admittedly the petitioner is a citizen of Bangladesh temporarily residing in U.S.A. where she went along with her husband for higher study in medicine and appointed her brother-in-law Abu Tayeb Akhand as her constituted attorney to look after the property and to do all acts for protection of the same. It further appears that when the first notice dated 24.8.72 was served to handover possession within 7 days the petitioner informed all the facts regarding her title and possession of the property to the S.D.O. (South). Dhaka who after making necessary inquiry and investigation through on 15.8.76 again a notice was served upon the father-in-law of the petitioner to handover possession of the property to the Superintending Engineer, Abandoned Houses Circle, Dhaka. The petitioner once again informed the authority concerned regarding the property and its ownership and possession. On being satisfied again it was cancelled on 2.9.76. Then about 3 years after on 20.11.79 Ministry of Public Works served another notice in the name of her constituted attorney to surrender possession. Whereupon the petitioner through her attorney filed objection reiterating all facts regarding the title, owner-ship and possession asserting that the petitioner is a citizen of Bangladesh temporarily living in U.S.A. It was also asserted that the property was not an abandoned property whereupon Ministry by its order bearing No. XVII/Dacca-9/79/330 dated 28.5.80 served a notice to handover possession otherwise the petitioner shall be evicted. Upon receipt of the aforesaid order the petitioner filed Title Suit No. 591/80 subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 86 of 1987 for a 'declaration as aforesaid impleading the respondents as defendants. Ultimately the suit was dis-missed ex-parte. As against that a First Appeal was preferred being P.A. No. 143 of 1989 and relating all these admitted facts and there is no denial.
